content:
You can rehearse the music, finish the lyric slides, and test the stream while still missing permission for what you plan to share. Settle those permissions before your first public service so volunteers know what belongs on the screen and online.

This guide covers U.S. copyright basics for worship music and films. Use it to prepare questions for a licensing provider or copyright attorney. It does not determine whether a particular use is lawful.

---

## Understand the religious-service exemption

Under 17 U.S.C. 110(3), the following is exempt from copyright infringement:

> performance of a nondramatic literary or musical work or of a dramatico-musical work of a religious nature, or display of a work, in the course of services at a place of worship or other religious assembly;

That covers qualifying performances and displays during a religious service. It does not grant permission to make copies. Creating lyric slides or printing song sheets raises a separate reproduction question, even when the display during worship qualifies for the exemption.

The House report explains that the exemption does not extend to transmissions to the public or to showing motion pictures in sequence. It also excludes social, educational, fundraising, and entertainment activities from this particular exemption. Other exceptions may apply, but being a church does not settle every use.

<Callout type="warning">
A worship service in a rented auditorium can qualify. Do not assume the building's license covers your church, or that your service exemption covers a concert, movie night, or public stream.
</Callout>

---

## Map what you will actually use

Make a list before buying a license. Start with the service plan, then include rehearsals, the lobby, and anything you will post later.

| Planned use | What to check |
|---|---|
| Live congregational singing | Whether the service exemption applies |
| Lyric slides or printed songs | Permission to reproduce the exact song |
| Music performed by your team online | Streaming and archive permissions |
| Backing tracks or an artist's recording online | Song and recording coverage |
| Film scene or movie night | Title, venue, audience, and exhibition permission |
| Worship clip in a promotional video | Permission for that separate use |

A song and a particular recording of it are different works. Check both when using recorded music. Put anything uncertain on a question list rather than treating a successful download as permission.

---

## Cover lyrics and music copies

CCLI's Church Copyright License permits specified copying of covered songs for congregational singing, including digital projection. Its terms require song validation, reporting when required, and copyright credits. It does not authorize copying every score, choir arrangement, or instrumental work.

ONE LICENSE offers reprint permissions for covered congregational music in bulletins and projections. Its reprint license excludes music for choirs, ensembles, accompanists, and instrumentalists. Check the publisher and the particular material before making copies.

For your music team, identify the edition you intend to use and ask whether that use is covered. Buy authorized copies or obtain permission for excluded material. Keep the credit information with the slides and handouts so volunteers do not have to reconstruct it on Sunday.

---

## Separate streaming from recording rights

CCLI's Streaming License extends its Church Copyright License to covered songs performed live by church musicians online. Streaming Plus adds coverage for authorized master recordings, backing tracks, and multitracks. Validate the song and recording rather than assuming every track you own qualifies.

ONE LICENSE's Podcast / Streaming options distinguish streaming alone from a bundle that includes reprint rights. Its Limited option does not permit sharing lyrics or melody lines with viewers. Its separate Recorded Audio License can cover specified recordings when paired with Podcast / Streaming permission. Ask the provider to confirm your exact combination and tracks.

Check archived services as well as the live broadcast. Ask what must happen to existing videos if coverage ends. ONE LICENSE requires removal of material licensed under its Podcast / Streaming options when you do not renew.

<Callout type="important">
License descriptions were checked October 15, 2026. Before purchasing or renewing, confirm current terms, fees, catalog coverage, reporting, and archive rules with CCLI, ONE LICENSE, CVLI, or Swank, as applicable. Confirm U.S. law with the U.S. Copyright Office. Provider pages can change.
</Callout>

---

## Treat films as a separate permission

A film's religious theme does not bring its screening within the religious-service exemption. Check permission for a sermon scene and for a full movie before scheduling either.

CVLI's Church Video License covers participating content subject to its terms. Verify the title, any current exclusions, and the licensed location. CVLI says its license does not cover movie content in services streamed to the general public. Its support page describes limited closed or gated streaming permissions, so ask about the precise audience and platform rather than assuming a password is sufficient.

Swank also licenses films for religious organizations. Request permission for your specific event and follow its instructions for obtaining a legal copy. Tell the provider about publicity, admission, location, and online viewing before committing to the event.

---

## Choose coverage around your service plan

Compare coverage against the songs and media you actually intend to use. CCLI and ONE LICENSE are options to investigate, not automatic substitutes for each other. A license is useful only where its catalog and permitted activities match your needs.

Ask a provider to confirm coverage in writing for any doubtful item. Give the song title, writer, publisher, recording version, and intended use. For a film, give the title, event details, and audience.

<Callout type="tip">
Give one person responsibility for the permission list and a backup person access to it. Keep confirmations, license details, renewal dates, and reporting instructions together for the Worship Leader and production volunteers.
</Callout>

Before budgeting, request a current quote for your church and planned uses. Ask whether a sending church's or venue's agreement includes your plant. Record the answer instead of carrying over another organization's license number.

---

## Check the service before going live

Use a checklist with the final service plan:

- [ ] Verify each song, score, recording, and video against its permission.
- [ ] Add the credits and license notices required for slides, handouts, and streams.
- [ ] Check music before and after the service, including any lobby audio reaching the stream.
- [ ] Remove or replace material whose permission you cannot confirm.
- [ ] Test the online feed separately from the room's sound and screens.
- [ ] Record actual use and submit the provider's required reports.
- [ ] Check the posted recording and note its archive and renewal obligations.

YouTube warns that licensed content can still interrupt a live stream if the rights holder has not added the channel to its Content ID allowlist. Ask your provider about handling claims before the service. Keep a plan for continuing without the disputed material.

---

## Avoid shortcuts that leave gaps

Credit is not a substitute for permission. Owning a copy does not give you every reproduction or public-performance right. A music license also does not settle permission for every photo, Bible translation, video, or other item in a service.

Do not assume a short film clip is automatically fair use. U.S. law calls for weighing the purpose, nature, amount used, and market effect. Ask a copyright attorney when relying on that exception for a doubtful use.

Keep a dated record of the use you checked and the answer you received. Recheck when the repertoire, recording source, venue, or distribution changes. The next volunteer should be able to see why an item is cleared without repeating the research.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Whether, then, you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God."* — 1 Corinthians 10:31 (LSB)
</Callout>
excerpt: Check the permissions for worship music, lyric copies, streaming, recordings, and films before your church goes live.
title: Copyright Licenses for Worship and Streaming

sources.claim: 17 USC 110(3) quoted verbatim. Sections 102 and 106 distinguish musical works and recordings, reproduction and performance rights; section 107 lists the four fair-use factors. These support sections 1, 2 and 8, not a conclusion about any particular use.
sources.quote: performance of a nondramatic literary or musical work or of a dramatico-musical work of a religious nature, or display of a work, in the course of services at a place of worship or other religious assembly;

sources.claim: House Report 94-1476 explains section 110(3): religious gatherings can use auditoriums; no transmissions to public at large, sequential motion pictures, or social/educational/fundraising/entertainment activities under this exemption. Supports sections 1, 2 and 5.
sources.publisher: U.S. Government Publishing Office, House Report 94-1476
sources.quote: the exemption would not extend to religious broadcasts or other transmissions to the public at large

sources.claim: CCLI U.S. Church Copyright License permits specified copying for congregational singing and digital projection. Requires validation, credits and reports when required; excludes specified choir/solo/instrumental copying. Supports sections 2, 3 and operational checklist.

CCLI U.S. Streaming extends Church Copyright License for covered live church-musician performances; Streaming Plus adds authorized master recordings/backing tracks/multitracks. Provider recommends reading full terms. Supports section 4 and service-plan selection.
sources.quote: from any authorized source during your online services

sources.claim: ONE LICENSE reprint covers congregational music, not choir/ensemble/accompanist/instrumentalist music. Podcast/Streaming options distinguish bundled reprint from Limited, which excludes shared lyrics/melodies. Archives licensed under these options must be removed on nonrenewal; credits and reporting required. Supports sections 3, 4, 7 and 8.
sources.quote: Reprint Licenses are intended for congregational use only.

sources.claim: ONE LICENSE Recorded Audio can cover specified master and self-produced recordings and pair with Podcast/Streaming permission for streams. Verify exact recordings and combination because older streaming descriptions exclude commercial masters when considered alone. Supports section 4.

CVLI covers participating content subject to title exclusions, location and terms; no public-internet movie streaming, with limited closed/gated arrangements described separately. Supports section 5, planned-use inventory and screening questions.
sources.quote: The Church Video License terms do not cover streaming movie content

sources.claim: Swank offers religious-organization film licensing and directs event planners to obtain a legal copy if Swank is not supplying one. Supports section 5; event details are recommended questions, not a promise of a particular grant.
sources.quote: make sure to get your own legal copy of the film

sources.claim: YouTube live streams are scanned for third-party content and licensed streams can be interrupted without rights-holder Content ID allowlisting. Supports section 7; contacting provider and fallback plan are practical recommendations.
sources.quote: your live stream can be interrupted even if you’ve licensed the third-party content

sources.claim: 1 Corinthians 10:31 (LSB), checked individually on the official reader, exact quotation in scripture callout. No new theological interpretation.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation, Legacy Standard Bible
sources.quote: Whether, then, you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

rulings: Resolved editorial scope: U.S. law only; phase 0 follows the existing administrative/legal section because A11 has no phase.
Resolved editorial scope: compare permissions without endorsing a provider; omit fees, repertoire counts, numerical thresholds and blanket legal conclusions.
Resolved source wording: distinguish ONE LICENSE streaming alone from its current Recorded Audio pairing. Provider pages describe both, so do not state that it can never cover recordings.

Resolved source wording: CVLI public streams are excluded, while limited closed/gated arrangements require verification against exact provider terms. Do not imply every password-protected stream qualifies.
Resolved scripture choice: use individually verified 1 Corinthians 10:31 (LSB) as a standalone callout without adding theological or methodology claims.
Resolved related-article boundary: published equipment/capture advice does not itself clear copyright; this draft adds the permission checks without changing those published rows.
